title: Markets: Tuesday 27 October

morning.session_note: Weekday ASX edition · before the 10:00 open
summary: ASX 200 futures pointed about 0.1% higher before the open after the S&P 500 rose 0.7% to 7,676.8 and the Nasdaq 0.8%, with chip stocks up almost 3% on the day Anthropic filed for its IPO. December Brent settled 0.8% lower at US$115.81 as Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish officials held talks in Tehran ([AFR](https://www.afr.com/markets/equity-markets/asx-to-rise-wall-street-lifts-anthropic-files-for-ipo-20261027-p618s2), [Morningstar/Dow Jones](https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/202610266927/front-month-ice-brent-crude-fell-078-to-settle-at-11581-data-talk)).

For Australia, rate-hike pricing firmed before Wednesday's CPI: ASX 30-day interbank futures put the chance of a 3 November hike at 62% at Monday's close, up from 56% on Friday, and the AFR reported money markets at 65%. Citi says a hike is already all but locked in, while NAB still expects a hold ([RBA Watch](https://rbawatch.com/rba-meeting/november-2026), [AAP](https://aapnews.aap.com.au/news/rare-chance-to-see-reserve-bank-react-to-inflation-data)).

Next: Israel votes today, Governor Bullock's team faces Senate Estimates at 11:15am Wednesday as September-quarter CPI lands at 11:30am (market forecast 1.0% trimmed mean), the RBNZ decides at noon, and the Fed announces at 5am Thursday Sydney time, with CME FedWatch at about 10% for a hike this week ([Westpac Weekly](https://library.westpaciq.com.au/content/dam/public/westpaciq/secure/economics/documents/aus/2026/10/WestpacWeekly20261026.pdf), [InvestmentNews](https://www.investmentnews.com/equities/the-fed-meets-again-this-week-will-advisors-see-another-rate-hike/268742)).

cards.headline: Wall Street rises as Anthropic files to list and Meta raises cash for AI
cards.takeaway: Chip stocks rose almost 3% as Anthropic filed to list, and Meta set out plans to raise up to about US$95 billion in new equity.
cards.new_since_last_issue: All new. Monday's issue previewed megacap earnings; the Anthropic S-1, Meta's equity raise and Microsoft's buyout offer came overnight.
cards.what_happened: Anthropic filed its S-1 with the SEC to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, without setting a price range ([SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2130357/000162828026067168/anthropicpbc-sx1.htm), [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/news/s1-sec)). The filing shows first-half 2026 revenue of US$16.29 billion, up from US$1.16 billion a year earlier, and a first-half operating loss of US$693 million ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/26/anthropic-ipo-live-updates-ai-s-1-filing.html)). Meta launched about US$35 billion of stock and mandatory convertible preferred offerings and plans up to US$60 billion more through an at-the-market programme of its previously announced Class C shares, not expected to start before early 2027 ([Meta](https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2026/Meta-Announces-Launch-of-Offering-of-Depositary-Shares-Representing-Series-A-Mandatory-Convertible-Preferred-Stock-and-Offering-of-Class-A-Common-Stock-in-Connection-with-Forward-Sale-Agreements/default.aspx)). Some investors in the Anthropic deal have told bankers their fair-value estimate slipped to about US$1.4–1.5 trillion after the investor day, with some saying about US$1.75 trillion is achievable, Bloomberg reported ([AP via SMH](https://www.smh.com.au/business/markets/asx-set-to-edge-up-wall-street-climbs-anthropic-files-for-ipo-20261027-p618sc.html)). Microsoft offered voluntary exits to eligible staff in Canada, India, the UK and the US ([Microsoft](https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2026/10/26/introducing-a-voluntary-exit-offer/)); about 60,000 people, or 27% of its workforce, are eligible, according to a person familiar with the matter ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/26/microsoft-msft-voluntary-buyouts.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: AI stocks have swung on worries about the cost of borrowing to build data centres, according to AP. Meta said Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom have indicated interest in buying up to a combined US$5 billion of its offering; AP called that a signal of strong interest from chip companies that benefit from AI spending, but said it also gives fuel to critics of "circular financing" ([AP via SMH](https://www.smh.com.au/business/markets/asx-set-to-edge-up-wall-street-climbs-anthropic-files-for-ipo-20261027-p618sc.html)). Alphabet and Microsoft report on Thursday morning Sydney time.
cards.market_reaction: The S&P 500 rose 0.7% and the Dow 0.3% to 52,361.58 ([AP](https://apnews.com/article/wall-street-stocks-dow-nasdaq-693ac6c4e67da0332045e66804780be7)). The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was up almost 3% in afternoon trade ([AFR](https://www.afr.com/markets/equity-markets/asx-to-rise-wall-street-lifts-anthropic-files-for-ipo-20261027-p618s2)); Nvidia rose 2.5% and Meta ended 0.2% lower after swinging (AP via SMH). The VIX fell 1.05 points to 18.40 (snapshot, delayed).
cards.priced_in: The S&P 500 is within 1.6% of its record set earlier this month, according to AP.
cards.what_to_watch: Alphabet and Microsoft results on Thursday morning Sydney time, and when Anthropic sets a price range.

cards.headline: Oil eases from six-month highs as regional envoys meet in Tehran
cards.takeaway: Brent had its biggest one-day fall since 13 October but is still up almost 12% for the month, and analysts quoted by Reuters see risks still tilted higher.
cards.key_figure: December Brent settle US$115.81 (−0.8%) on Mon 26 Oct · WTI US$101.76 (CNBC)
cards.new_since_last_issue: Monday's close wrap had oil easing on Qatari mediation and flagged the contract roll in our data. New are the settlement, the Tehran meeting's outcome and the US reserve figure.
cards.what_happened: December Brent settled 91 cents, or 0.78%, lower at US$115.81 a barrel, its largest one-day fall since 13 October, though still up 11.86% for the month ([Morningstar/Dow Jones](https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/202610266927/front-month-ice-brent-crude-fell-078-to-settle-at-11581-data-talk)). It briefly topped US$117 during a session in which Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish officials met Iranian leaders in Tehran ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/26/oil-prices-today-wti-brent.html)); Reuters attributed the fall to hopes of easing US–Iran hostilities. The Houthis said they had struck pumping stations on Saudi Arabia's East-West crude pipeline and Riyadh airport, and Saudi Arabia said it had intercepted more missiles and drones ([Reuters via Euronext](https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/oil-drops-near-six-month-highs-hopes-iran-war-hostilities-ease)).
cards.why_it_matters: Fuel is part of the CPI basket; Wednesday's figures cover September and the September quarter, so October's prices bear on later readings and on the RBA's outlook for its 3 November decision. US Energy Department data showed the Strategic Petroleum Reserve at 282.6 million barrels, the lowest since 1982 ([Reuters via Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/articles/oil-prices-down-almost-1-232445179.html), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/26/oil-prices-today-wti-brent.html)).
cards.market_reaction: Gold futures rose 0.5% to US$4,026.2 (snapshot, delayed). The snapshot's Brent futures change is not usable today; see the comparison.

competing_views.view: "We therefore expect volatility to remain elevated, with risks still skewed to the upside."
"Any Brent price dips back to the lows of last week will find grateful buyers."

comparison.title: Did Brent fall 0.8% or 5.5% on Monday?
comparison.why_different: Different contracts. December Brent settled at US$115.81, down 0.78%. Our snapshot's continuous series (Yahoo BZ=F) has rolled to the January contract (about US$110.3) but compares it with December's Friday close of US$116.72, so its −5.5% is a contract-roll artefact. The January contract itself fell about 1.3%, from US$111.70 to about US$110.3, which is consistent with AP's report that the most actively traded contract returned to US$111.40 during the day. Don't use the snapshot's −5.5%.

cards.headline: ASX set to edge higher after Wall Street's tech rally
cards.takeaway: Futures point to a small gain at the open, ahead of Wednesday's CPI and Thursday morning's Fed decision.
cards.key_figure: ASX 200 futures 8,831 (+4 points, +0.1%) near 6am (AFR) · cash index closed Monday at 8,809.9 (+0.2%)
cards.new_since_last_issue: Monday's close wrap covered the session. The futures indication for today's open is new.
cards.what_happened: ASX 200 futures were up 4 points, or 0.1%, to 8,831 near 6am ([AFR](https://www.afr.com/markets/equity-markets/asx-to-rise-wall-street-lifts-anthropic-files-for-ipo-20261027-p618s2)); an earlier AP report had futures up 11 points, also 0.1% ([AP via SMH](https://www.smh.com.au/business/markets/asx-set-to-edge-up-wall-street-climbs-anthropic-files-for-ipo-20261027-p618sc.html)). The two figures were taken at different times. On Monday the ASX 200 rose 14.7 points to 8,809.9, more than 4% below its August record ([AFR](https://www.afr.com/markets/equity-markets/asx-to-fall-on-oil-spike-key-central-bank-rate-decisions-this-week-20261026-p618ht)). Correction: Monday's close wrap used pre-close readings. The official closes were ASX 200 8,809.9 (not 8,814.2), ZIP A$1.620 (not A$1.65) and CSL A$195.14 (not A$193.44).
cards.why_it_matters: Overnight US gains were led by chip stocks. Locally, Wednesday's CPI is the next scheduled input for RBA rate expectations (see the rates cards).
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard: ASX 200 8,809.9 (+0.2%), AUD US$0.7031 (+0.36%, RBA 4pm Monday), US 10-year 5.00% (unchanged), gold US$4,026.2 (+0.5%). ASX SPI futures and iron ore are not in our data feed.
cards.what_to_watch: The 10am open and IDP Education's AGM at 10am.

cards.headline: Hike odds firm a day before CPI and Bullock's Senate appearance
cards.takeaway: Markets lean towards a 3 November hike, and economists differ on how much Wednesday's CPI will change the outcome.
cards.key_figure: 62% chance of a 3 Nov hike in ASX 30-day interbank futures at Monday close, up from 56% on Friday (RBA Watch)
cards.new_since_last_issue: Monday's close wrap had the 62% reading. New are the AFR's 65% money-market figure, its report that a hike is fully priced early next year, and the Citi and NAB views.
cards.what_happened: ASX 30-day interbank futures implied a 4.76% cash rate after the 3 November meeting at Monday's close, a 62% chance of a 25bp hike from 4.60% ([RBA Watch](https://rbawatch.com/rba-meeting/november-2026)). Money markets imply a 65% chance, with a hike fully priced early next year ([AFR](https://www.afr.com/markets/equity-markets/asx-to-fall-on-oil-spike-key-central-bank-rate-decisions-this-week-20261026-p618ht)). The two figures come from different measures and are shown separately, not averaged.
cards.why_it_matters: The RBA's August forecasts implied quarterly trimmed-mean inflation of about 0.8%, against the 1.0% market forecast for Wednesday, according to AAP ([AAP](https://aapnews.aap.com.au/news/rare-chance-to-see-reserve-bank-react-to-inflation-data), [Westpac Weekly](https://library.westpaciq.com.au/content/dam/public/westpaciq/secure/economics/documents/aus/2026/10/WestpacWeekly20261026.pdf)). Governor Bullock and her team appear before Senate Estimates at 11:15am Wednesday, 15 minutes before the release.
cards.market_reaction: Australian 2- and 10-year yields in our feed lag to 21 October and are not used here.

competing_views.who: Josh Williamson and Faraz Syed, Citi
competing_views.view: Expect a 1.0% trimmed mean but call the November outcome a "lay-down misère", saying even 0.9% would get the board over the line on a hike.
Also forecasts a 1.0% trimmed mean but expects a hold at 4.60%, citing below-trend growth and a gradually easing labour market.

cards.what_to_watch: Bullock's opening remarks at 11:15am and the trimmed mean at 11:30am Wednesday, measured against 0.8% (RBA's implied path) and 1.0% (market forecast).

cards.headline: Futures point to a Fed hold on Thursday and a December hike
cards.takeaway: Fed funds futures put a 10.5% chance on a hike this week and more than 80% on at least one hike by December.
cards.key_figure: CME FedWatch: 10.5% chance of a hike this week; more than 80% for at least one hike by December (InvestmentNews, 26 Oct)
cards.new_since_last_issue: Monday's issue cited Friday's pricing via CNBC. New are Monday's FedWatch odds and a soft two-year Treasury auction.
cards.what_happened: As of Monday afternoon US time, CME FedWatch put the odds of a quarter-point hike this week at 10.5%, down from 33.8% on 14 October. For December it showed a 73.1% chance of 4.00–4.25% and 8.3% for 4.25–4.50%, putting the odds of at least one hike by year-end above 80% ([InvestmentNews](https://www.investmentnews.com/equities/the-fed-meets-again-this-week-will-advisors-see-another-rate-hike/268742)). The Treasury sold US$69 billion of two-year notes at 4.708%, slightly above the 4.705% when-issued yield, with a bid-to-cover of 2.59 against 2.63 at the previous auction ([Dow Jones via MarketScreener](https://ca.marketscreener.com/news/u-s-2-year-treasury-auction-shows-slightly-softer-demand-ce785cdcdf8ff72c)).
cards.why_it_matters: The decision is at 5am Thursday Sydney time, six days before the US midterms. Westpac also expects a hold this week and a 25bp hike in December ([Westpac Weekly](https://library.westpaciq.com.au/content/dam/public/westpaciq/secure/economics/documents/aus/2026/10/WestpacWeekly20261026.pdf)).
cards.market_reaction: US 2-year 4.68% (−1bp) and US 10-year 5.00% (unchanged), Treasury par curve for Monday (snapshot).

competing_views.view: Expects "tough talk on the inflation front combined with soft action", saying bond markets have already tightened credit conditions.
Questions whether a longer hiking cycle is coming because so much inflation is energy-related and could ease if the conflict is resolved.

cards.what_to_watch: The statement and press conference from 5am Thursday Sydney time, especially any signal on December.

cards.headline: Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish envoys hold first joint talks in Tehran
cards.takeaway: Iran says the four countries agreed to keep talking, while Saudi Arabia said the visit supports de-escalation.
cards.key_figure: First joint meeting of Iran and the three Mecca pact states (Iranian state TV, via Al Jazeera)
cards.new_since_last_issue: Monday's issues reported the trip was planned. The meeting's outcome and the statements from both sides are new.
cards.what_happened: Saudi Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin met President Pezeshkian and Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei. A joint statement said the participants "agreed to continue talks to strengthen cooperation among the four regional countries" ([Tehran Times](https://www.tehrantimes.com/news/531543/Pezeshkian-to-Turkey-Pakistan-Saudi-officials-Iran-seeks-cooperation)). Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey had not commented on the meeting or the reported agreement by the time Al Jazeera published. Earlier on Monday, Saudi deputy minister Rayed Krimly said the visit supports "de-escalation" and the mediation by Qatar and Pakistan ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/26/officials-from-mecca-pact-states-to-hold-talks-in-iran-amid-regional-tensions)).
cards.why_it_matters: Saudi Arabia, a major oil exporter, has faced weeks of Houthi attacks, and the pact treats an attack on one member as an attack on all (Al Jazeera). Pezeshkian said Iran "will firmly defend" the rights of the Iranian nation and reserves the right to peaceful nuclear activity (Tehran Times).
cards.market_reaction: Brent settled lower on the day of the talks (see the oil card).
cards.what_to_watch: Any Saudi or Turkish readout, and whether the Houthis keep attacking Saudi targets.

cards.headline: US forces ready for major Iran strikes if Trump orders them, CNN reports
cards.takeaway: Officials told CNN that Trump has not decided and that any order is more likely after the 3 November midterms; the White House declined to comment.
cards.key_figure: Strikes possible "within 96 hours" of an order (two US officials, via CNN)
cards.new_since_last_issue: New since Monday's morning issue, which had Trump weighing a deal or strike.
cards.what_happened: CNN, citing two US officials, reported that US forces could launch new, potentially major operations against Iran within 96 hours of an order, with a target list that includes energy infrastructure, military sites and nuclear facilities. Officials said Trump had not decided and a go-order was most likely after the midterms. The White House declined to comment ([CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/10/26/politics/us-iran-strike-plans-trump)). The account rests on CNN's unnamed sources; Iran International and Ynet carried CNN's report rather than confirming it independently ([Iran International](https://www.iranintl.com/en/202610265046), [Ynet](https://www.ynetnews.com/article/syzzmfnhmg)).
cards.why_it_matters: The reported target list includes energy infrastructure. CNN also reported that US officials asked Israel to hold off on its own strikes; Netanyahu's office called "fake news" an Israeli source's account that he had sought a joint attack before Israel's election. On Sunday Trump told Fox News it was "getting to be decision time" on strikes or a deal ([Investing.com](https://au.investing.com/news/economy-news/catalystfilled-trading-week-ahead-oil-prices-ease--whats-moving-markets-4713736)).
cards.market_reaction: No separate market move was attributed to the report.

competing_views.view: Said the status quo around the Strait of Hormuz is "untenable" for the long term without a diplomatic breakthrough.
Said the idea that Iran can be forced into surrender "is a false and void notion".

cards.what_to_watch: White House statements after the midterms on 3 November, and any ordered departures from more US embassies in the region.

cards.headline: Brazil's markets fall sharply after Lula's re-election
cards.takeaway: The Ibovespa fell 13.88% after a circuit-breaker halt and the US dollar rose 8.21% against the real; analysts quoted by Brazilian and international outlets linked the moves to fiscal concerns.
cards.key_figure: Ibovespa −13.88% to 176,608.23 · US dollar +8.21% to R$5.403 (InfoMoney)
cards.new_since_last_issue: Monday's close wrap had the result. The market reaction and Flávio Bolsonaro's challenge are new.
cards.what_happened: The Ibovespa closed 13.88% lower at 176,608.23 after the first circuit-breaker halt since March 2020. The Treasury cancelled this week's fixed-rate and inflation-linked bond auctions and bought back about R$7.1 billion of fixed-rate notes. The US dollar rose 8.21% to R$5.403, its fifth-largest daily gain since the 1994 Real Plan ([InfoMoney](https://www.infomoney.com.br/mercados/ibovespa-hoje-bolsa-de-valores-ao-vivo-26102026/)). Flávio Bolsonaro did not concede and said he would seek to annul the result, objecting to a Supreme Court minister's two-hour extension of voting. Electoral court president Kassio Nunes Marques said he had "absolute confidence" in the electoral process ([G1](https://g1.globo.com/politica/eleicoes/2026/noticia/2026/10/25/flavio-resultado-segundo-turno.ghtml), [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/10/26/brazils-real-sinks-after-lulas-re-election-victory)).
cards.why_it_matters: Brazil is Australia's main rival in seaborne iron ore. Vale rose 4.01%, one of only eight Ibovespa stocks to gain, all of them exporters, which InfoMoney linked to the dollar's rise.
cards.market_reaction: Vale +4.01% and Suzano +10.08% while most of the index fell (InfoMoney).

competing_views.view: Said Lula's win "will dash hopes for reforms that would improve the public finances and strengthen growth prospects".
Said the real is "still likely to be supported by strong commodity revenues" and that "the scale of the victory suggests that the result will stand".

cards.what_to_watch: How Brazil's electoral court handles any annulment request, and any fiscal signals from Lula's team.

rba.summary: A 62% chance of a 25bp hike on 3 November in ASX 30-day interbank futures at Monday's close (expected rate 4.76%), up from 56% on Friday. The AFR reported money markets at 65%. Prediction markets (Polymarket and Kalshi, as compiled by RBA Watch) showed 68%.

forecasts.view: Expects a hike in November, saying even a 0.9% trimmed mean would be enough.
Expects a hold at 4.60% despite forecasting a 1.0% trimmed mean.
Expects a 25bp hike in November to 4.85% if CPI is broadly in line with its forecast.

fed.summary: CME FedWatch put a 10.5% chance on a hike this week from the 3.75–4.00% range. For December it showed 73.1% for 4.00–4.25% and 8.3% for 4.25–4.50%, so more than 80% for at least one hike (as reported by InvestmentNews on Monday afternoon US time).

forecasts.view: Expects a hold this week and a 25bp hike in December.

No new verified news since the chair succession covered in Monday's close wrap. The shares fell 0.8% to A$195.14 (snapshot).
No new verified news. The shares fell 1.4% to A$11.09 (snapshot).
AGM today at 10am. A filing late Monday showed State Street becoming a substantial holder at 5.39% as of 22 October. The shares rose 0.9% to A$2.23 (snapshot).
